details.advice: If possible, avoid this date. A weekday earlier in the term or after finals would likely draw better attendance, especially for first-years who may be busy with end-of-semester obligations.

sponsorship.email_body:
Hi [Sponsor name],

I’m reaching out from our student club to ask if you’d consider supporting our Outdoor Movie Night on the Quad for first-year students. We’re planning an evening of community-building with an inflatable screen, popcorn, hot chocolate, blankets, and a short welcome from our club before the film.

We’d love to partner with you as a sponsor and can offer recognition in our event promotion and at the event itself. Any support would make a big difference in helping us create a warm, welcoming experience for new students.

If you’re open to it, I’d be happy to share more details or discuss a sponsorship amount that works for you.

Thank you for your time and consideration,
[Your name]

timeline.title: Setup crew arrives
timeline.detail: Unload screen, projector, sound gear, blankets, seating, and food supplies at the Main Quad.

timeline.title: Set up seating and check-in

timeline.title: Food station prep
timeline.detail: Warm hot chocolate, set out popcorn, and place allergy/ingredient labels in view.

timeline.title: Doors open
timeline.detail: Welcome attendees, confirm headcount, and point students to seating and refreshments.

timeline.title: Club welcome
timeline.detail: Maya gives the short introduction and welcomes first-year students before the film.

timeline.title: Movie starts

phases.name: Phase 1: 4 Weeks Out
phases.subtitle: Secure the quad, movie, and funding targets

tasks.title: Reserve Main Quad and confirm power access
tasks.detail: Lock in the Main Quad reservation for 2026-12-11, confirm the nearest approved power source, and check any noise or access limits for an 8–10 PM outdoor screening.

tasks.title: Pick the film and verify screening rights
tasks.detail: Choose a movie that works for first-years and confirm the club can publicly screen it on the quad, including any rental or licensing needs.

tasks.title: Build sponsor ask list and packet
tasks.detail: Prepare a simple funding ask for the campus department, student government/alumni group, and nearby café, with a clear request tied to the $1,100 gap.

tasks.title: Launch finals-aware promotion to first-years
tasks.detail: Promote the event through dorm RAs, first-year group chats, and club socials, framing it as a low-effort study break because early December and Friday timing may reduce turnout.

tasks.title: Collect dietary needs and allergy notes
tasks.detail: Ask attendees and volunteers about allergies or dietary restrictions, then decide how popcorn ingredients, butter, and hot chocolate add-ins will be labeled and separated.

tasks.title: Confirm food-serving approval and safe setup
tasks.detail: Check what the club needs to serve popcorn and hot chocolate on the quad, including sanitation, cups, serving tools, and any campus food-service clearance.

tasks.title: Trim purchases to stay inside the lean budget
tasks.detail: Compare expected headcount against the $400 cap and decide where to save if sign-ups run light, especially on food quantity and blanket count.

tasks.title: Finalize welcome script and film intro
tasks.detail: Write a short club welcome for the start of the night, including a quick introduction for first-years before the movie begins.

tasks.title: Confirm sponsor support and pickup plan
tasks.detail: Follow up on sponsor asks, confirm any donated coffee shop supplies or cash support, and plan who will pick up or receive each item.

tasks.title: Test AV, power, and screen stability
tasks.detail: Run through the projector, speakers, and inflatable screen setup, including cords, anchors, and weights for the expected evening wind.

tasks.title: Confirm volunteer stations and call times
tasks.detail: Assign specific people to check-in, food line, roaming support, and cleanup so the team is ready for a 150-person outdoor crowd.

tasks.title: Send final reminder to first-years
tasks.detail: Post one last reminder with the start time, Main Quad location, and a note to bring a blanket or light jacket for the cooler evening.

tasks.title: Buy and pack food service supplies
tasks.detail: Purchase and pack popcorn, hot chocolate mix, cups, stirrers, napkins, ingredient labels, hand sanitizer, and trash bags for the food table.

tasks.title: Print signage and check-in materials
tasks.detail: Prepare entrance signs, food labels, the check-in sheet, and a simple seating map so guests can find the lawn area quickly.

tasks.title: Reconfirm venue access and campus contacts
tasks.detail: Double-check the access window for the quad, the exact outlet location, and the on-call campus contact in case anything changes at setup.

phases.name: Wrap-Up: 1-3 Days After
phases.subtitle: Return rentals, close out costs, and thank everyone

tasks.title: Return rentals and strike equipment
tasks.detail: Load out the projector gear, inflatable screen, cords, and any borrowed items, then confirm everything is returned in good condition.

tasks.title: Reconcile receipts and close the budget
tasks.detail: Match all purchases and sponsor support against the $400 budget, note the actual spend, and flag any reimbursement issues.

tasks.title: Send thank-yous and collect feedback

compliance.title: Outdoor space reservation and sound approval

compliance.title: Food service and hot beverage handling

compliance.title: Student event registration and safety contact
compliance.detail: Check whether the club must register a 150-person outdoor event and provide a contact list or basic safety plan for the evening.

title: Fall Hackathon 2026
concept: A 24-hour hackathon with three keynote workshops, mentor office hours, a midnight pizza run, sponsor booths and project demos with judging. Needs overnight building access, strong Wi-Fi and enough power for every team.
time_window: 24h overnight, Fri 6 PM to Sat 6 PM
plan_summary: The plan is well structured across prep phases, event-day operations, and wrap-up, with all major event needs assigned and scheduled. Main residual risk is execution under a lean budget, especially around sponsor fundraising and overnight operational coverage, but the plan does address those areas.

goals: Run a 24-hour hackathon with workshops, mentoring, and demos
Provide overnight space with reliable Wi‑Fi and power for teams
Host sponsor booths, project judging, and a final demo session
must_haves: Overnight access to the Engineering Building, Hall B
Enough power outlets/charging for every team
open_questions: How many sponsor booths and teams should the space be planned for?
Who will serve as judges and mentors?

steps.summary: Indoor event for student hackers and project teams, overnight, with food.

details.advice: This is a pretty good date overall: no nearby holiday conflict and it’s not near a major semester crunch point. If you can, schedule it earlier in the day or make it hybrid/flexible to catch students before weekend plans start.
conflicts: Friday can reduce turnout a bit, especially if the event depends on daytime campus spaces or students who leave town for the weekend.

steps.summary: Friday 2027-01-29: no public holidays within a week. Risk: low.

savings_ideas: Ask sponsors or local pizza shops to cover the midnight meal and provide in-kind snacks/drinks.
Request university IT/facilities support for Wi‑Fi, extra power strips, and overnight security so cash can go to food and judging instead of rentals.
Reuse existing campus tables, signs, extension cords, and AV gear, and keep workshops low-cost with volunteer speakers and digital materials.

Because the event is overnight and needs strong Wi‑Fi, enough power, food, and an indoor/after-hours backup plan, outside sponsorship or in-kind support would materially improve the experience.

sponsorship.email_body:
Hi [Sponsor name],

I’m [Your name] from the student club organizing Fall Hackathon 2026 on January 29–30 in the Engineering Building. We’re bringing together about 180 student hackers for a 24-hour event with workshops, mentoring, demos, and sponsor booths.

We’d love to partner with you as a sponsor to help cover event costs like food, Wi‑Fi/power support, and mentor/judge hospitality. In return, we can offer recognition on event materials, booth space, and visibility with engaged student participants.

Would you be open to discussing a sponsorship of $[amount]?

Thank you for considering it, and I’d be happy to share more details.

Best,
[Your name]
